card.title: Cricothyrotomy
card.subtitle: Scalpel, bougie, tube. A palpable membrane.
card.blurb: The transverse stab technique from the Difficult Airway Society 2025 card, on a normal adult neck.

review: Not physician reviewed. Steps follow the DAS 2025 eFONA action card, transverse stab incision, as quoted in each step. The geometry is teaching geometry, not measured anatomy. Depth and volume ranges are teaching choices.

field.note: The drapes cover the chest below the clavicles and the face above the chin. The whole neck is bare from side to side: the trapezius, the fossae above the clavicles and the clavicles themselves show.

sources.cite: Difficult Airway Society. eFONA action card, Plan D: transverse stab incision. DAS 2025.
sources.note: Read 28 October 2026. Step wording is quoted from the card and its teaching framework.

sources.cite: The height of the cricothyroid membrane on computed tomography scans in trauma patients. 2017.
sources.note: Mean height about 7.9 mm in men and 6.0 mm in women. The model's membrane is about 9 mm high. Citation details unverified.

sources.cite: Savva test, sternomental distance. e-Learning Anaesthesia (e-SAFE).
sources.note: "A distance of less than 12.5 cm is associated with difficulty." Used for the model's proportions.

sources.cite: Airway assessment and difficult airway identification. Open Exam Prep, CCP-C study guide.
sources.note: "Normal TMD: >6.5 cm." A secondary source. Used for the model's proportions.

hands.stretch: Stretching the skin and fixing the larynx.
hands.scalpel: Holding the scalpel, gentle traction toward you.

layers.name: Deep tissue
layers.note: Shown only in the midline cut, where it fills the space behind the airway. Not modeled anatomy.

layers.name: Head
layers.note: A union of simple solids at landmark positions (make_cric_head.py). Only a shape for the drape. Not anatomy.

layers.name: Trunk
layers.note: A shape for the drape to rest on (make_cric_torso.py). Not anatomy.

skin.feel: The skin parts under the blade.

ctm.feel: A give as the membrane parts.

lumen.feel: Loss of resistance. Air bubbles through the blood.

thyroid_cartilage.feel: Hard cartilage. The blade will not go through.

cricoid_arch.feel: A hard ring. The blade will not go through.

zones.name: Cricothyroid membrane
zones.feel: A soft dip in the midline, between the lower edge of the thyroid cartilage and the firm ring below it.

zones.name: Off the midline, beside the membrane
zones.feel: The dip is here but you are off the midline, over muscle.
zones.wrong: Off the midline. Come back to the center of the dip.

zones.name: Lower edge of the thyroid cartilage
zones.feel: A hard edge with a dip just below it.
zones.wrong: This is the lower edge of the thyroid cartilage. The membrane is the dip just below it.

zones.name: Cricoid cartilage
zones.wrong: This is the cricoid ring. The membrane is the dip just above it.

zones.name: Laryngeal prominence
zones.feel: The laryngeal prominence, the most anterior point of the thyroid cartilage.
zones.wrong: This is the laryngeal prominence. Slide down the cartilage to the dip below it.

zones.name: Thyroid notch
zones.feel: A V-shaped notch at the top of the thyroid cartilage.
zones.wrong: This is the thyroid notch, at the top of the larynx. The membrane is below the cartilage.

zones.name: Thyroid cartilage
zones.feel: Hard cartilage, the side of the thyroid cartilage.
zones.wrong: This is the thyroid cartilage. The membrane is below its lower edge.

zones.name: Hyoid bone
zones.feel: A hard bar high in the neck.
zones.wrong: This is the hyoid, too high. Come down past the thyroid cartilage.

zones.name: Over the thyroid isthmus
zones.feel: Soft, slightly full tissue over the upper tracheal rings.
zones.wrong: This is over the thyroid isthmus, too low. Come back up above the cricoid ring.

zones.name: Tracheal rings
zones.wrong: These are the tracheal rings, too low.

zones.name: Suprasternal notch
zones.wrong: This is the bottom of the neck, far too low.

zones.name: Sternocleidomastoid
zones.feel: A firm band of muscle running down and in toward the sternum.
zones.wrong: This is the sternocleidomastoid, at the side. The larynx is in the midline.

zones.name: Sternocleidomastoid
zones.feel: A firm band of muscle running down and in toward the sternum.
zones.wrong: This is the sternocleidomastoid, at the side. The larynx is in the midline.

zones.name: Clavicle
zones.feel: A firm bar of bone running out to the shoulder.
zones.wrong: This is the clavicle. The membrane is in the midline of the neck, well above it.

zones.name: Supraclavicular fossa
zones.feel: A soft hollow above the clavicle, the trapezius behind it.
zones.wrong: This is the hollow above the clavicle, at the side of the neck. The larynx is in the midline.

zones.name: Clavicle
zones.feel: A firm bar of bone running out to the shoulder.
zones.wrong: This is the clavicle. The membrane is in the midline of the neck, well above it.

zones.name: Supraclavicular fossa
zones.feel: A soft hollow above the clavicle, the trapezius behind it.
zones.wrong: This is the hollow above the clavicle, at the side of the neck. The larynx is in the midline.

zones.name: Side of the neck
zones.feel: Soft tissue at the side of the neck, away from the larynx.
zones.wrong: Too far to the side. The larynx is in the midline.

tools.name: Index finger
tools.desc: Your non-dominant index finger, for finding the membrane.

tools.name: Scalpel, size 10
tools.desc: A broad blade, about the width of the tube.

tools.name: Bougie with angled tip
tools.desc: The angled (coudé) tip lets you steer it.
tools.note: Teaching choices: the tract angle keeps the shaft inside the membrane opening, the bend radius is what the airway has room for.

steps.label: Declare CICO and the need for front of neck access
steps.prompt: Say it out loud: can't intubate, can't oxygenate. You need a front of neck airway.
steps.why: Naming it moves the team on from the upper airway. The card's first line is "Declare CICO and need for front of neck airway".

steps.label: Make sure help is here
steps.prompt: Call for help.
steps.why: "Ensure help is present."

steps.label: Confirm full neuromuscular blockade
steps.prompt: Confirm the patient is fully paralyzed.
steps.why: "Confirm full neuromuscular blockade."

steps.label: Keep oxygenating from above
steps.prompt: Keep trying to oxygenate through the upper airway while you work.
steps.why: "Ensure attempts to oxygenate via upper airway are maintained": facemask, high flow nasal oxygen or a supraglottic airway.

steps.label: Extend the neck, pillow under the shoulders
steps.prompt: Extend the neck fully. Put a pillow between the shoulder blades.
steps.why: "Maximal neck extension, no rotation" and "Pillow between scapulae" bring the larynx forward.

steps.label: Where do you stand?
steps.prompt: Choose your side of the patient.
steps.wrong: Stand on the side that puts your dominant hand free: the left side if you are right-handed, the right side if you are left-handed.
steps.why: "If right-handed: on the left side of the patient. If left-handed: on the right side."

steps.label: Laryngeal handshake, non-dominant hand
steps.prompt: Grip the larynx between thumb and fingers with your non-dominant hand.
steps.why: The laryngeal handshake identifies and holds the larynx. "Perform laryngeal handshake with left hand" (for a right-handed operator).

steps.label: Find the cricothyroid membrane
steps.prompt: Run your index finger down the midline. Click the cricothyroid membrane.
steps.why: "Locate CTM with left index finger." It is the soft dip between the thyroid cartilage above and the cricoid ring below.

steps.label: Stretch the skin, fix the larynx
steps.prompt: Stretch the skin over the membrane with your thumb and middle finger.
steps.why: "Stretch skin over CTM using left thumb and middle finger." A stretched, fixed target does not move under the blade.

steps.label: Transverse stab incision
steps.prompt: Set the cutting edge toward you. Click the membrane, then press and hold Push until you feel the give and air.
steps.why: "Make transverse stab incision with cutting edge towards operator." Keep the scalpel perpendicular to the skin. One stab goes through skin and membrane.

errors.edge_far: The cutting edge faces away from you. The card says the cutting edge faces toward the operator.
errors.edge_vertical: The blade is turned along the neck. This technique starts with a transverse stab.
errors.shallow: Not in the airway yet. Push again.
errors.deep: Too deep: the blade reached the back wall of the larynx. Pull back into the airway.
errors.resist: The blade met cartilage and will not go through. You are not on the membrane.

steps.label: Turn the blade 90 degrees
steps.prompt: Keep the blade perpendicular and turn it 90 degrees so the cutting edge points to the feet.
steps.why: "Twist blade through 90° (blade points towards feet) creating triangular hole."

errors.head: The cutting edge points to the head. Turn it the other way, toward the feet.

steps.label: Gentle traction toward you, handle upright
steps.prompt: Pull the scalpel gently toward you, handle upright.
steps.why: "Traction on scalpel towards you, handle upright." This opens the hole for the bougie.

steps.label: Swap hands: scalpel in your non-dominant hand
steps.prompt: Swap hands. Hold the scalpel with your non-dominant hand and keep the traction.
steps.why: "Swap hands maintaining traction." Your dominant hand is now free for the bougie.

steps.label: Bougie in along the blade
steps.prompt: Hold the bougie near its angled tip, parallel to the floor and across the neck. Press and hold Push to slide the tip in along the blade.
steps.why: "Position bougie parallel to floor and at right angles to the trachea. Insert bougie using scalpel blade as a guide."

errors.deep: The tip hit the back wall. With the shaft still across the neck the tip cannot go down the trachea. Turn it.
errors.early_turn: Get the tip into the trachea first, then turn.

steps.label: Turn the bougie toward the feet
steps.prompt: Turn the bougie through 90 degrees so it lines up with the trachea, tip toward the feet.
steps.why: "Rotate bougie to align with trachea." On the card: "Insert and rotate through 90 degrees, towards feet".

errors.head: The tip now points to the head, toward the vocal cords. Turn it toward the feet.

steps.label: Advance the bougie 10 to 15 cm
steps.prompt: Press and hold Push to advance. Release, then press Done when the bougie is 10 to 15 cm in.
steps.why: "Advance (to 10-15 cm). Note that clicks or hold up may be present." The clicks are the tracheal rings.

errors.short: Not far enough. The card says 10 to 15 cm.
errors.long: Too far. You may be at the carina or in a main bronchus. Pull back to 10 to 15 cm.

steps.label: Remove the scalpel
steps.prompt: With the bougie in, take the scalpel out.
steps.why: "Advance to 10cm-15cm and remove scalpel."

steps.label: Stretch the skin and steady the trachea
steps.prompt: Non-dominant hand: stretch the skin and stabilize the trachea.
steps.why: "Stabilise trachea and tension skin with non-dominant hand."

steps.label: Railroad the 6.0 cuffed tube
steps.prompt: Railroad the tube over the bougie. Rotate it as you advance. Stop when the cuff is inside the trachea, then press Done.
steps.why: "Rotate tube over bougie as it is advanced." Rotating stops the tube catching at the membrane.

errors.catch: The tube catches at the membrane. Rotate it as you advance.
errors.cuff_out: The cuff is not inside the trachea yet. It would leak.
errors.deep: Too deep. The tip is near the carina. Pull back.

steps.label: Remove the bougie
steps.prompt: Hold the tube and take the bougie out.
steps.why: "Remove bougie, inflate cuff & ventilate."

steps.label: Inflate the cuff
steps.prompt: Press and hold Inflate to fill the cuff. Release, then press Done.
steps.why: An inflated cuff seals the airway so ventilation goes to the lungs. The volume range here is a teaching choice.

errors.low: The cuff is soft. There will be a leak.
errors.high: The cuff is overfilled. Too much pressure on the tracheal wall.

steps.label: Ventilate and confirm with waveform capnography
steps.prompt: Attach the bag and ventilate. Look for a waveform on the capnograph.
steps.why: "Ventilate: confirm waveform capnography." A sustained waveform confirms the tube is in the trachea.

steps.label: Check the tube depth and secure it
steps.prompt: Check the depth of the tube and tie it in.
steps.why: "Check depth of tube and secure."

distractors.label: Make a vertical skin incision
distractors.feedback: A vertical incision is the technique for a membrane you cannot feel. This one can be felt, so it is the transverse stab.

distractors.label: Try a needle cricothyroidotomy
distractors.feedback: This exercise teaches the scalpel technique.

distractors.label: Try another intubation
distractors.feedback: Once CICO is declared, the next step is front of neck access.

distractors.label: Wait for an anesthesiologist
distractors.feedback: Help is called, but front of neck access does not wait.

points: The membrane is the soft dip between the thyroid cartilage and the cricoid ring. Find it by touch with the laryngeal handshake.
One transverse stab with the cutting edge toward you, then a turn so the edge points to the feet.
The blade guides the bougie. Turn the bougie toward the feet once the tip is in, and advance to 10 to 15 cm.
Rotate the tube as you railroad it. Confirm with waveform capnography.

proportions.note: Suprasternal notch to chin tip 14 cm (sternomental, normal over 12.5 cm). Thyroid notch to chin tip 7 cm (thyromental, normal over 6.5 cm). Teaching choices.
